summary: Creates a UDP socket (AF_INET/SOCK_DGRAM/IPPROTO_UDP), binds it to the first available local port in the range [hostshort, hostshort+100], then connects it to the GameSpy master server. Host string a2 is resolved into a sockaddr_in per candidate port; a resolved loopback address (127.0.0.1) is zeroed so the bind picks an explicit local address. On success calls sub_561D40 to prepare the socket object and returns the result of sub_561FF0(aMasterOpenspyN, 27900, object+236), which completes the master-server connection. Returns 1 if socket creation fails and 2 if binding (or getsockname when port 0 was requested) fails.

local_names.a1: optional output dword; zeroed on entry if non-null
local_names.a2: host string resolved per candidate port
local_names.hostshort: base local port; bind range start
local_names.v10: output pointer a1 or default object pointer global off_5E4DFC
local_names.v12: current candidate port in the bind scan
local_names.name: sockaddr_in built by sub_562010 and used for bind/getsockname
local_names.a4_a10: opaque arguments passed through to sub_561D40

operations.description: Save a1 into v10 and, if a1 is non-null, write 0 through it (output-initialization)
Call NetworkStartup() to initialize the Winsock/network subsystem
Create socket with socket(2, 2, 17) = AF_INET, SOCK_DGRAM, IPPROTO_UDP
Initialize the port scan: v12 = hostshort (start of the bind range)
Build sockaddr_in for the current candidate port: sub_562010(a2, v12, &name, 0)
Compute htonl(0x7F000001u), the loopback address in network byte order
If the resolved address equals loopback, zero the address field so the bind uses the local interface rather than 127.0.0.1
Bind the socket to the candidate address/port: bind(v11, &name, 16)
While bind fails, increment the candidate port v12 and retry until a bind succeeds or v12 reaches hostshort+100
If the whole bind range failed (v12 advanced past the range, non-zero), return 2
When the requested port was 0 (v12 == 0), set namelen to 16 and call getsockname(v11, &name, &namelen) to learn the OS-assigned port; return 2 if it fails
Read the bound port back with ntohs(*(u_short*)name.sa_data) (result is discarded)
Prepare the socket object: sub_561D40(v11, v11, a4, a5, a6, a7, a8, a9, a10)
If no output pointer was supplied, use the default object: v10 = &off_5E4DFC
Complete the master-server connection: return sub_561FF0(v11, aMasterOpenspyN, 27900, *v10 + 236)

unresolved: Arguments a4..a10 are passed through verbatim to sub_561D40 with unknown meaning.
The value *v10 + 236 handed to sub_561FF0 is a field at offset 236 of the network socket object; its identity is unknown.
The ntohs(getsockname) result is computed and discarded; the port-0 branch appears vestigial.
Return codes 1 and 2 distinguish socket-creation vs bind/getsockname failure, but the caller's interpretation is not evidenced here.
The overflow check on hostshort + 100 wraps the candidate port in an undefined way; semantics of the unsigned-overflow path are not resolvable from the raw text.
